data.optical_policy: At280nm in water use composition-based molar epsilon=5500*nTrp+1490*nTyr+125*nCystine in M^-1 cm^-1. Compare two declared endpoints for each uploaded chain: every Cys reduced, or all possible intrachain Cys pairs oxidized. Ignore other chromophores and modifications; do not infer the actual redox state from a sequence. Use canonical free-terminus average reduced-chain mass; each disulfide removes2.01588g/mol relative to that composition. Beer-Lambert A=epsilon*c*l, l=1cm. Report the two mass concentration conversion coefficients in g/L per unit A280 and the fractional molarity underestimate if an actually fully reduced chain were interpreted using its fully oxidized epsilon: (true molarity-estimated molarity)/true molarity. The redox-sensitivity acceptance limit is0.05. Return every candidate meeting that criterion; this criterion concerns redox sensitivity alone, not overall measurement accuracy.
data.scientific_scope: This is a retrospective theoretical reporting audit for deposited ubiquitin and crambin sequences, not measured absorbance, an instruction to manipulate redox state, or an empirical calibration. Composition-derived coefficients can have substantial error, especially without tryptophan. No absolute concentration accuracy guarantee follows from the redox-sensitivity comparison.
